scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8879: Users in both pods report that no internal portal
loads by NAME anymore -- web0.local through web3.local all fail with
name-resolution errors. Loading a portal directly by its IP address (e.g.
http://10.200.0.3) still works, and pings to 10.200.0.2 succeed. Diagnose.

injection.action: stop the BIND (named) DNS service on dns_server

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: dns_server BIND (named) DNS service
Mechanism: the named daemon on dns_server (10.200.0.2) has been killed, so
  nothing answers on port 53 and every *.local lookup from the pods times
  out -- which is why the portals fail by name. Everything else is healthy:
  the host 10.200.0.2 itself is up and pingable, the OSPF path works, and
  the web servers keep serving HTTP (portals load when addressed by IP).
  The symptom is purely dead name resolution.
Localization: dns_server
Root cause: named not running on dns_server (port 53 closed)
Fix: `systemctl start named` on dns_server
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the BIND DNS service on dns_server (e.g. `systemctl start named`).
Once named is answering again, web0.local..web3.local resolve to their
10.200.0.x addresses and the portals load by name. The web servers and the
network need no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: BIND/named DNS service down (name resolution dead, port 53 closed)
bonus-rules-out-network: notes 10.200.0.2 is reachable and portals load by IP, so the network and web servers are healthy -- only resolution is broken

agent.diagnosis_text:
The BIND9 name server (`named`) was never started on `dns_server`, leaving TCP/UDP port 53 closed and returning "connection refused" to every DNS query. Because clients' `/etc/resolv.conf` points exclusively to `10.200.0.2` for name resolution, all symbolic lookups (`web0.local` through `web3.local`) fail with resolution errors — while direct-IP access and ICMP pings to `10.200.0.2` succeed because those require no DNS.

The root cause is a missing daemon-start command in the Kathara device startup script. Kathara containers run with `/bin/bash` as PID 1 (confirmed on the live device), so systemd never executes; the `named.service` symlink in `/etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/` is completely inert. The service is marked *enabled* but was never launched. Both the zone file (`/etc/bind/db.local`, verified with `named-checkzone`) and `named.conf` are syntactically correct and contain the right A records (web0 → 10.200.0.3, web1 → 10.200.0.4, web2 → 10.200.0.5, web3 → 10.200.0.6). When `named` was started manually during this investigation (`named -g -u bind`), it bound to `10.200.0.2:53` and immediately resolved all four names correctly.

Corrective fix: Add `service named start` (or equivalently `/usr/sbin/named -u bind`) to the `dns_server.startup` file in the lab directory so the daemon is launched at container initialisation time. No changes to zone data or named.conf are required.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names `dns_server` as the affected device multiple times (e.g., 'never started on `dns_server`').

per_axis.axis: must-identify-component: BIND/named DNS service down (name resolution dead, port 53 closed)
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies that the BIND (`named`) daemon on dns_server is not running, leaving port 53 closed and causing DNS name resolution to fail.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-network: notes 10.200.0.2 is reachable and portals load by IP, so the network and web servers are healthy -- only resolution is broken
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states 10.200.0.2 is reachable (ICMP/direct-IP access) and portals load by IP, confirming the network and web servers are healthy and only DNS resolution is broken.
Recommends starting the named/BIND daemon (and adding it to the container startup), which matches the expected fix to run/restart the DNS service.

The agent's logs show missing/closed port 53, valid configs, manual start succeeding, PID 1 = bash (no systemd), and absence of startup scripts — the writeup's conclusions follow directly from those observations.
